entries.title: Treasury designates a Tren de Aragua financial network it says laundered ATM jackpotting proceeds through cryptocurrency, and lists Tron addresses on the SDN entries
entries.facts: Treasury press release sb0640, dated September 30, 2026, announces sanctions on a financial network of the foreign terrorist organization Tren de Aragua. The release states that "Among other methods, the network designated today uses cryptocurrency transactions to launder proceeds of ATM jackpotting," and separately that "Among other methods, Prometheus uses cryptocurrency transactions to launder proceeds of ATM jackpotting attacks." The designations are made under Executive Order 13581, as amended, and Executive Order 13224, as amended. Nine individuals are designated, including Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre, identified in the release by the alias "Prometheus," and Juan Gabriel Rivas Nunez, alias "Juancho." Two entities are designated: Enigma Community, S. de R.L. de C.V. and Soluciones Integrales Toluca, S.A. de C.V. The corresponding OFAC recent-actions entry, headed "Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations Designations; Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations Removals," carries the field label "Digital Currency Address" eight times and lists seven Tron (TRX) addresses against designated individuals. The same entry records designation removals for Patraca, S.A. de C.V., the vessel Maraya, and Tatyana Protopovich.
entries.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury press release sb0640 (September 30, 2026)
entries.relevant_to: exchanges, custodians, stablecoin issuers, banks, card and ATM networks, payment processors, sanctions compliance teams

entries.title: SEC settles a same-day block of administrative orders against operators and promoters of unregistered offshore CFD brokerages whose customers funded accounts with Bitcoin or other crypto assets
entries.facts: The SEC issued a sequential block of settled administrative orders on September 30, 2026, File Nos. 3-22759 through 3-22766. Four were retrieved in full. Release 34-106544 (File 3-22765) finds that Anthony Tyler Williams co-owned and operated KOT4X, an unregistered online brokerage, from 2019 to 2025, solicited U.S. retail investors to trade security-based swaps in the form of contracts for differences based on stocks, marketed the platform through social media and recruited affiliates, and that approximately $296 million was deposited into customer accounts. It states: "To trade, customers registered on the KOT4X website, funded their trading accounts with Bitcoin or other crypto assets that were custodied in a margin account by the white-label service providers, and then received access to trading products." It finds a violation of Section 15(a)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and imposes a $125,000 civil money penalty and a two year associational bar with a right to apply for reentry. Release 34-106538 makes parallel findings against Quillan Black, a social media influencer known as "Cue Banks," as a co-owner and operator of KOT4X, with the same penalty and bar. Release 34-106539 makes parallel findings against Tyler MacKechnie as to Envi LLC, with an $85,000 penalty payable in three installments over one year and a two year bar. Release 34-106540 makes parallel findings against Jordan Morgan as to Prosperity, and states that approximately $35 million was deposited into customer accounts. In each retrieved order the stock-based contracts for differences are found to be security-based swaps under the federal securities laws. Three further orders in the same block, Releases 34-106541, 34-106542 and 34-106543, were not retrieved.
entries.source_label: SEC administrative order, Release No. 34-106544, File No. 3-22765 (September 30, 2026)
entries.relevant_to: trading platforms, CFD and derivatives venues, crypto on-ramps, affiliate and influencer marketing programs, broker-dealer compliance teams

entries.title: Treasury's Stablecoin Certification Review Committee interim final rule publishes with dates filled in: effective September 30, 2026, comments due November 30, 2026
entries.facts: Federal Register document 2026-19966, "Forms and Procedures for Review of State Certifications by the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee," RIN 1505-AC97, docket TREAS-DO-2026-0562, published on September 30, 2026. Its DATES section reads: "Effective date: This interim final rule is effective September 30, 2026; however, certifications will not be accepted until after Paperwork Reduction Act approval of the information collection. Treasury will post a notification on its website as to when certifications will be accepted. Comment date: Comments on this interim final rule must be received on or before November 30, 2026." The published SUMMARY states that Treasury is issuing the rule on behalf of the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee, that the Committee is adopting interim procedural regulations and forms to implement its responsibilities under section 4(c) of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act, and that the regulations set out a process to facilitate the Committee's approval or denial of certifications submitted by State payment stablecoin regulators under section 4(c)(4) and prescribe the form of such certifications. The SUMMARY adds: "This interim final rule will ensure that interim forms and procedural regulations are in place to facilitate submission of certifications by the effective date of the GENIUS Act, and the Committee intends to revise these forms and procedural regulations, as appropriate, following consideration of comments."
entries.source_label: Federal Register document 2026-19966, U.S. Department of the Treasury interim final rule (published September 30, 2026)
entries.relevant_to: payment stablecoin issuers, state payment stablecoin regulators, banks and their stablecoin subsidiaries, payment processors

entries.title: OFAC's Cuban Assets Control Regulations amendments take effect, removing the U-turn funds transfer authorization, alongside five new and twenty-nine amended Cuba FAQs and an OFAC Alert
entries.facts: Federal Register document 2026-19973, an OFAC final rule amending the Cuban Assets Control Regulations, published on September 30, 2026. Its DATES section reads: "This rule is effective September 30, 2026." Its SUMMARY states that OFAC is amending the regulations to implement portions of the President's foreign policy toward Cuba, including as directed by National Security Presidential Memorandum-5, signed June 30, 2025, and that "Among other things, this rule adds a prohibition on indirect financial transactions with entities or subentities on the Cuba Restricted List; amends other authorizations related to financial transactions, including removing an authorization for 'U-Turn' transactions; and amends authorizations related to travel and related transactions, including removing authorizations for group people-to-people travel and professional meetings in Cuba." The OFAC recent-actions entry for the action enumerates the guidance issued with it: five new Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions, numbered 1271 through 1275; twenty-nine amended Frequently Asked Questions; and an OFAC Alert titled "Expanded Sanctions Against Cuba," which the entry describes as highlighting increased sanctions risks for transactions involving Cuba. The entry also records that the accompanying regulatory package removes duplicative provisions and reorganizes multiple parts of the Code of Federal Regulations, eliminating over 100 subparts. The texts of the individual FAQs were not retrieved.
entries.source_label: Federal Register document 2026-19973, OFAC final rule (published September 30, 2026)
entries.relevant_to: banks and money transmitters handling cross-border funds transfers, payment processors, correspondent banking and sanctions compliance teams

entries.title: CFTC secures a court order in the Fundsz digital assets and precious metals fraud action directing over $31 million in restitution and penalties
entries.facts: CFTC press release 9305-26, dated September 30, 2026, states that the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida entered an order against Brian Early of Louisiana and Alisha Ann Kingrey of Arkansas directing them to pay $15,732,455 in restitution and a $15,752,455 civil monetary penalty. The release describes the underlying conduct as "a digital assets and precious metals fraud involving the unincorporated Fundsz entity and its website," states that participants were told their "money would be traded according to a proprietary algorithm," and states that Fundsz's founder and controlling person "had deceived participants into investing in Fundsz." The release further states that consent orders were entered involving Rachel Larralde, representing the estate of Rene Larralde, and Juan Pablo Valcarce, and that the Larralde estate is directed to relinquish to a court-appointed receiver a personal residence purchased with investor funds together with over $2.7 million in other assets. The release names the court but the retrieved page did not state a case number.
entries.relevant_to: digital asset platforms and pooled investment programs, exchanges, compliance and marketing teams

entries.title: SEC settles an order against a BitConnect lending-program promoter, finding unregistered offers and sales and unregistered broker activity, with a twelve month suspension
entries.facts: SEC Release No. 34-106553, File No. 3-22766, dated September 30, 2026, finds that Trevon Brown offered and sold unregistered investment contracts representing interests in the BitConnect lending program from April 2017 to January 2018, promoted those investments through online videos and at BitConnect events, and received transaction-based compensation for direct sales together with recruiter commissions from his downline, without being associated with a registered broker or dealer. The order finds violations of Sections 5(a) and 5(c) of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 15(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It imposes a suspension from association with any broker, dealer, investment adviser, municipal securities dealer, municipal advisor, transfer agent or nationally recognized statistical rating organization for twelve months. No monetary penalty is specified in the order.
entries.source_label: SEC administrative order, Release No. 34-106553, File No. 3-22766 (September 30, 2026)
entries.relevant_to: token issuers, lending and yield programs, affiliate and referral marketing programs, promoters and influencers
